paper.title_en: On a Dual Heterotic Kodaira-Spencer Theory
paper.abstract_en: We consider a dual version of heterotic Kodaira-Spencer theory on a Calabi-Yau three-fold $X$ with background fluxes, related to the type I BCOV theory of Costello-Li. We implement the Green-Schwarz mechanism of Costello-Li, where the Beltrami differential plays the role of the Green-Schwarz field. On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.
